prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a production sprite atlas for God Sandbox, Early Stone Age, eight individually designed functional structures. The input image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its exceptionally dense small pixel clusters, three-quarter top-down view, tiny material texture details, restrained warm natural palette, top-left light, right/down shadows and crisp hand-authored pixel-art appearance. Create a NEW transparent-background atlas, precisely 4 columns x 2 rows, eight isolated sprites in equal cells, with generous fully transparent gutters and no text, labels, grid or border. Top row left to right: (1) irregular A-frame branch-and-bark survival shelter, no finished door or masonry; (2) open flint-knapping canopy with raw timber stakes, stone table and baskets of stone; (3) timber logging camp with a low bark roof and stacked raw logs; (4) rough stone gathering camp, rubble supports, split rocks and simple timber shade. Bottom row left to right: (5) raised primitive food/material storage rack with a bark cover and woven baskets; (6) communal branch meeting canopy, open sides and rough log seating; (7) earth-covered charcoal clamp, cut logs protruding at edge, tiny vents, no metal; (8) cold-climate low domed branch shelter covered with overlapping bark and earth, heavy rough stone windbreak. Every silhouette must differ substantially. No medieval houses, chimneys, sawn brick, metal fasteners, modern machinery, nails or decorative fake tools. Rich bark grain, individually lashed poles, tiny fibre ties, irregular stones, chipped flint, packed-earth contact and small tufts, no square grass platform. Match the original detail density and camera angle. These must read as premium 96px-wide pixel sprites, not vector, low poly, blurry icons or cartoon flat shapes. Frame each entire object completely within its cell. Produce at 1536x1024 or higher with each sprite centred in its own cell.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one game production atlas in EXACTLY 4 columns by 2 rows, transparent background, equal cells with clear gutters, eight complete isolated Agricultural Age building sprites. STYLE REFERENCE: copy the original reference sheet's dense finely crafted pixel-art detail, overhead three-quarter perspective, top-left illumination, down-right small shadows, natural irregular ground contact and coherent material rendering. Do not copy medieval masonry, tiles, chimneys or metal. Top row left to right (1) wattle-and-daub family house, timber frame, steep detailed thatch, clay walls; (2) large communal timber longhouse, steep thatch, open porch; (3) raised granary on short rough stone piers with thatch, wicker grain bins and simple wooden stair; (4) pottery workshop with a rounded clay firing kiln, drying clay vessels, firewood, open wooden awning. Bottom row (5) weaving workshop, open timber frame, loom and hanging woven fibre cloth under reed roof; (6) carpenter's timber work yard, rough sawing frame, worked beams and hand tools under a deep thatch awning; (7) compact desert adobe family house with shaded courtyard and flat earthen roof, only timber/clay/stone/fibre, no glass or metal; (8) tropical high-stilt family house with steep palm-thatch roof, bamboo walls, ventilated porch, individually lashed beams. Distinct purpose and silhouettes, finely drawn wall weave, roof fibres, timber grain, weathering and small construction joints, highly detailed pixel clusters. Premium pixel art for 64-80px logical sprites. No labels/text/grid, no square grass bases, no vector shapes, no low-poly or simple cartoon buildings, no modern elements. Each sprite wholly within its own cell, same view angle and density, no overlap. At least 1536x1024.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE production pixel-art sprite atlas for God Sandbox. Reference image: style reference only, match its dense hand-authored-looking pixels, top-down three-quarter camera, crisp clusters, top-left light, restrained earthy palette and bottom-right contact shadows. Create a transparent 4-column by 3-row atlas at 1536x1536, TWELVE complete isolated building sprites, centred in equal cells with wide truly transparent gutters. Do not put any pixels in neighbouring cells. No labels, text, border or grid. Each structure must be distinctive and detailed when exported at 64 logical pixels wide; no vector, low-poly, cartoon boxes, blurry surfaces or square grass bases. Tiny material texture, grain, lashings, weathered clay, individual thatch and masonry, organic contact with ground. EXACT order: row 1 col1 Early Stone Age fibre/cordage twisting canopy, rough poles and bark cover with coils of plant-fibre rope and hand twisting stakes, no loom; col2 Agricultural timber carpentry yard, deep thatch awning, timber beams, a raw stone adze and flint hand-scrapers, NO metal saw or metal blade; col3 Agricultural grain-grinding shelter, reed roof over saddle quern stones, grain baskets and sacks, hand-driven only, NO waterwheel or machinery; col4 Agricultural shaduf irrigation station, lashed-timber counterweight pole, stone counterweight and clay bucket, a small clay-lined water channel, open access to water, no mechanised pump. Row 2 col1 Bronze Age compact adobe/mudbrick courtyard home with flat earthen roof, timber lintels and shaded entrance, no glass; col2 Bronze Age smelting workshop with two low rounded clay furnaces, leather bellows, clay crucibles and moulds, green copper ore and charcoal baskets, UNLIT dark furnace openings; col3 Bronze Age bronze tool workshop with a stone anvil, small clay hearth, moulds and bronze axe heads with timber handles, no iron anvil, no modern tongs or machinery, UNLIT hearth; col4 Bronze Age ore mine entrance in a small natural rock outcrop, heavy lashed timber supports, green copper and grey tin-bearing rocks and carrying baskets, no rails, minecart or iron. Row 3 col1 Bronze Age public mudbrick granary, stone pier foundation, flat timber-and-earth roof, large grain bins, ventilation slots; col2 Bronze Age mudbrick market court, open fabric awnings, baskets and traded goods, humble clay/stone floor with organic terrain edges; col3 Bronze Age civic meeting hall, substantial mudbrick walls, timber roof beams, low earth roof and open gathering portico with wooden benches, NO European town-hall clock, tower, tiles or medieval features; col4 Bronze Age masonry yard, open timber shade, dressed stone blocks, stacked clay bricks, hammerstones and wooden levers. All buildings use plausible stone, timber, plant fibres, mudbrick, clay and Bronze Age metal where specified. Never use iron, concrete, steel, electrical elements, steam machinery, Renaissance/classical columns or European medieval architecture. Very detailed pixel-art style coherent with the original reference, not a realistic 3D render. Keep the whole building and props inside each cell with transparent separation.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single transparent-background God Sandbox Agricultural Age farm enclosure game sprite. Match the reference sheet's dense premium pixel art, top-down three-quarter camera, top-left light, crisp detailed pixel clusters and warm earthy restrained palette. Show one compact wattle-and-timber farmyard, low reed-thatch seed-store shelter on rough stone pads, carefully lashed wooden fence and gate, two empty tilled-earth beds, a wooden hoe, seed baskets and water jar. Empty tilled beds only: NO live crops, fruit, grain heaps or growing plants within the beds. No metal, medieval tiled roof, glass, windmill, waterwheel, modern tools or machine. Precise small roof fibres, timber grain, wicker texture, worn clay and individually chipped stones. Whole object isolated on real alpha transparency, natural irregular ground contact with no square grass platform, substantial clear transparent margins. This will be packed at up to 64x64 logical pixels to a 2x2 terrain footprint; preserve dense readable detail and architectural style, not low-poly or flat cartoon shapes.

packing: tools/pack_architecture.py exports up to 64x64 logical pixels for 2x2 terrain footprints; generation is stochastic, committed-source packing is deterministic.
